entry.title: I built a free VS Code extension that catches leaked secrets before you commit them
entry.summary:
The problem
Last year I nearly committed a Stripe live key to a public repo. Caught it manually at the last second. But it made me think — So I built EnvGuard. EnvGuard is a free VS Code extension that adds 6 things your 🔐 Secret Scanner — detects 30+ patterns (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Stripe keys, JWT tokens) with red underlines before you commit ✅ Schema Validation — define a .env.schema file, get instant errors for missing/wrong keys 🔄 Environment Switcher — save dev/staging/prod profiles, switch with one click 🔍 Diff Viewer — compare any two .env files side by side 📋 Example Generator — auto-generate .env.example from your real .env 🖥️ Dashboard — visual overview of all keys, security score, profiles Add this to your .env: EnvGuard immediately shows a red wavy underline and adds to Works for 30+ secret types including AWS, GitHub, Stripe, Google, Create a .env.schema file: DATABASE_URL=required|url|description:PostgreSQL connection string EnvGuard validates your .env against this in real time. VS Code Marketplace: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=GayathriS.envguard-pro GitHub (open source): https://github.com/GayathriCodes2/EnvGuard.Extenstion This is my first published VS Code extension. If you try it If it's useful, a ⭐ on GitHub genuinely helps.
